instructions: Finely chop the onion and grate half the carrot on the small holes of a box grater. Put them in a large bowl.

Finely chop 1/2 cup of the parsley and 3 tbsp of the dill. Add them to the bowl with the 1 lb ground beef, the 1/4 cup rice, 1 of the eggs, the 2 tbsp olive oil, the 1 tsp salt, the pinch of coriander and the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Knead it with your hands for a minute or two, until it's smooth and holds together. Put the bowl in the fridge for 15 minutes. It's easier to roll when it's cold.
Meanwhile, bring the 4 cups chicken broth to a boil in a wide pot.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into balls about the size of a walnut. That should make about 20.
Turn the heat down so the broth simmers gently. Lower the meatballs in one at a time with a spoon. If they aren't covered, add warm water until they are.
Cover the pot and simmer for 25 minutes, until the rice in the meatballs is tender. Skim off any foam that rises. Cut one open to check: the rice should be soft and there's no pink in the middle.
While they simmer, juice the 2 lemons. That should be about 1/3 cup. Whisk the other 2 eggs in a bowl until they're frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice.
Take the pot off the heat. Whisking the whole time, slowly pour a ladle of the hot broth into the eggs. Add a second ladle the same way. Go slowly, or the eggs will scramble.
Pour the egg mixture into the pot and swirl the pot gently to mix it in without breaking the meatballs.
Set the pot over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring gently, until the broth turns silky and slightly thick. Don't let it boil, or the sauce will curdle.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley. Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Ladle the soup into bowls and scatter the parsley over the top.
method_notes: All three versions mix ground beef with raw rice, onion, egg and fresh herbs, poach the meatballs about 25 to 30 minutes, and finish the soup with eggs and lemon juice tempered with hot broth. My Greek Dish (the lead) uses parsley, dill, a little grated carrot and a pinch of coriander, rests the mixture 15 minutes, and cooks the meatballs in water; Dimitra's Dishes and Real Greek Recipes cook them in chicken broth or stock, and Dimitra adds cornstarch to the egg-lemon. This follows the lead's meatballs and avgolemono at its own 4 servings but poaches them in chicken broth for a fuller-tasting soup.
